questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
What is likely to be the short-run consequence of replacing central planning with a market-based system?

options.A: a decrease in the rate of inflation
options.B: a lower rate of return on capital investment
options.C: a more equal distribution of income and wealth
options.D: an increase in the level of unemployment

What is an externality created by an individual consuming take-away food?

options.A: the cost to the individual of purchasing the take-away food
options.B: the litter created by the individual’s take-away food packaging being discarded
options.C: the pleasure derived by the individual from eating the take-away food
options.D: the time saved by the individual purchasing the take-away food

questions.questionText: A project has a social cost of $100 million, a private cost of $40 million and an external benefit of $20 million. Its net social value is zero. What can be concluded about the project?

options.A: External cost is greater than external benefit.
options.B: Private cost is greater than external cost.
options.C: Private cost is greater than private benefit.
options.D: Social cost is greater than social benefit.

questions.questionText: What is least likely to be included in a cost-benefit analysis of a proposed new university?

options.A: the costs of building the new university
options.B: the extra income earned by the new university’s graduates
options.C: the future staffing costs of other universities
options.D: the staffing costs of the new university five years into the future

questions.questionText: Which argument is an importer most likely to use to gain the support of consumers for free trade?

options.A: More imports allow the government to raise revenue from tariffs.
options.B: More imports improve the country’s terms of trade.
options.C: More imports increase competition in the domestic economy.
options.D: More imports raise total employment in the domestic economy.

options.A: a credit in the capital account
options.B: a credit in the current account

options.D: a debit in the current account

options.A: The economy experiences a period of deflation.
options.B: The general level of prices is falling.
options.C: The growth of money supply falls below the growth of output.
options.D: The rate of inflation is positive.

questions.questionText: What would most help a country to achieve a surplus on the current account of the balance of payments?

options.A: a depreciating exchange rate combined with a high rate of inflation and falling productivity
options.B: a depreciating exchange rate combined with a low rate of inflation and rising productivity
options.C: an appreciating exchange rate combined with a high rate of inflation and falling productivity
options.D: an appreciating exchange rate combined with a low rate of inflation and rising productivity
